solution: Count the complement: strings of length n over 26 letters that avoid p. Build the KMP automaton of p and keep only its |p| non-accepting states; the number of avoiding strings is the row sum of T^n applied to the start state, where T[s][t] counts letters moving s to t without completing a match. |p| <= 50 and n <= 10^12, so raise the transfer matrix by binary exponentiation, about 40 squarings of a 50x50 matrix. The answer is 26^n - avoid, all arithmetic mod M. O(|p|^3 log n) time, O(|p|^2) space; M is an arbitrary modulus up to 10^12, so products need 128-bit arithmetic and no inverses may be used.
statement_summary: Given a length n, a modulus M and a pattern string p of at most 50 lowercase letters, the task is to count the lowercase strings of length n that contain p somewhere as a substring, reported modulo M. The length reaches 10^12 and the modulus 10^12, so up to twenty such datasets must each be answered without enumeration.
notes: Both samples match (1 and 52) and full enumeration over alphabets of size 2 and 3 agrees on 120 random (n, p, M) with n up to 11. M is not necessarily prime, which rules out any division-based shortcut; the transfer-matrix route needs none.
